statements: Section 45(1)(c) of the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 requires Scottish Water to send its statement of accounts to the Auditor General for Scotland for auditing, by such time as the Scottish Ministers may direct.

Section 21(2) of the Public Finance and Accountability (Scotland) Act 2000 requires an account that must be sent to the Auditor General for auditing to be sent not later than 6 months after the end of the financial year to which it relates, which supplies the deadline the 2002 Act leaves to direction.

Section 45(1)(b) of the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 requires Scottish Water to prepare for each financial year a statement of accounts giving a true and fair view of the state of its affairs and its income and expenditure.

Section 45(2) of the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 requires every statement of accounts to comply with any direction of the Scottish Ministers as to the information it contains, the manner in which that information is presented, and the methods and principles according to which it is prepared.
Section 45(1)(a) of the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002 requires Scottish Water to keep proper accounts and accounting records.
